themes.name: Livelihoods after arrival
themes.gist: The paid and unpaid work immigrants performed once in the new country, from mines and packing plants to domestic labor and pre-arranged farm work.
code_names: Domestic labor as only work after arrival
Family trade carried forward to new country

themes.name: Regional networks as settlement aid
themes.gist: How immigrants from the same village or home region clustered in American towns and relied on one another to adjust.

themes.name: Costs and conditions of departure
themes.gist: The bureaucratic hurdles, fare manipulations, home-currency economies, and pressures such as conscription that shaped how and why immigrants left.
code_names: Barter and farm surplus as economy

themes.name: The toll of migration and labor
themes.gist: The wear on bodies, housing, and families that the journey, the work it required, and the separations it imposed inflicted on immigrants.
code_names: Children kept from school to work in family business
Children left behind during staged migration
